newsitem.title: UK: UK utilities off as report pegs windfall 5 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK utilities off as report pegs windfall 5 bln stg.

text.p: Shares in UK utility and water companies eased in early trading on Friday after the Financial Times said the government's windfall tax would total some five billion stg.
The greatest burden would fall on British Telecommunications Plc, which would pick up one billion stg of the tax tab, the paper said.
BT shares dropped 5p to 450-1/2p at 0748 GMT.
In the electricity sector, National Power Plc dropped 4p to 520-1/2p, while PowerGen Plc fell 3-1/2p to 717-1/2.
Among gas distributors, BG Plc was off 6p to 228p, while Centrica Plc eased 1/4p to 77-1/4.
Water stocks, which rebounded on Thursday, also slipped back. Thames Water Plc was down 3-1/2p to 689, and South West Water Plc eased 6p to 706-1/2.

"No one really knows, but even if it's five billion, it's still in line with what the market had been expecting," said Greig Middleton, an analyst with Gordon Culfeather. "The devil will be in the detail."
"I think market makers are just using that story as an opportunity to mark shares down," he added.
Shares in BAA Plc firmed 4-1/2p to 556-1/2 as the Financial Times' influential Lex Column said the airport operator was expected to come out a winner.
Analysts said the one billion figure that would hit BT seemed high.

"But one thing is certain, if the windfall tax is set too high, it's more likely to be challenged," said another analyst, who asked not to be named. "It will be a difficult balancing act for the government."
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown is set to unveil his first budget on July 2
